featured_reviews.name: Sviren
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited a small restaurant called Malvan, and it truly felt like a home away from home. The food had an authentic Malvani flavor, with rich spices that made every dish stand out.

I ordered the Veg Thali, which was priced at just ₹200, and it was absolutely worth it. The thali included Bharleli Vangi (stuffed brinjal), Malvani ussal, solkadi, gulab jamun, bhakri, and chapati — all freshly prepared and full of flavor.

I have never liked brinjal before, but after tasting the Bharleli Vangi here, I was genuinely impressed — it completely changed my opinion!

The restaurant itself is small, but very charming and cozy. The yellow-themed interior creates a warm and beautiful atmosphere that adds to the overall experience.

The only small drawback was that the chapati was slightly cold, but everything else was excellent and made up for it.

I would highly recommend this place to anyone who enjoys homestyle food. Whether you are vegetarian or non-vegetarian, this place offers a delightful and authentic Malvani dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Raghav Kukreti
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a first time traveller in Mumbai, I didn't know any good restaurants, went here because it was recommended by friends and what can I say other than it's honestly the best seafood I've had in my life.

I've already gone again in 2 days and plan to go again before leaving. The fish is extremely fresh; as a newcomer I told the server that I didn't know what to order except I knew I wanted to eat tandoori crab. They were extremely helpful, kept checking in if everything was okay and the service was a 10/10.

I ate tandoori crab and a pomfret thali the first day. Crab was 10/10 spicy very flavorful and they were helpful enough to break the claws. The pomfret was succulent, flaky, no offensive flavors. Even my wife who is mostly vegetarian ate the fish like she's been eating it for years. A huge testament to this restaurant.

The second time we ate Bangda and Rawas thalis. Both were amazing. The bangda fish was so good we ended up ordering a second order of 2 bangda frys. Another 10/10.

Had modak as dessert which was also soft, juicy and just lovely. The kokam soda is also the best way to cleanse your palate.

In closing I would like to say, if you have any desire to eat seafood, this place is a blind go. You cannot go wrong with anything you order. 100/10.

owner_posts.post_text:
The Surmai Fish Thali at Malwani Kkalwan is the meal that makes the case for authentic Malvani food Mumbai before the first bite even reaches the table — surmai fried to a proper crisp, a sharp Malvani fish curry built on coconut and kokum, served alongside bhakri, chapati, amboli, and steamed rice in the kind of full spread that a one-dish order simply cannot replicate on its own no matter how good that single dish happens to be on its own merit alone. This is Konkani coastal cooking the way it has been made for generations along the Konkan coast, not a shortened version built for speed and convenience at the cost of flavour.

It sits at the centre of why Malwani Kkalwan continues to hold a genuinely strong position for authentic Malvani food Mumbai — a thali built around surmai rather than assembled from whatever happened to be available that particular day, served at an address in Aram Nagar that has become the destination for seafood lovers across Versova, Lokhandwala, Yari Road, and Andheri West. Sol Kadi on the side rounds out the meal exactly the way it should, cooling the palate between every bite of fish curry along the way through the entire meal served.

For anyone searching for authentic Malvani food Mumbai or an authentic Konkani restaurant Mumbai with a proper fish thali worth the trip across the city — Malwani Kkalwan on JP Road, near Seven Bungalows Garden, is that address.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Bharat Balvalli
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was an extremely disappointing, frustrating, and unacceptable experience.

We had ordered 2 Surmai Thalis, and the gravies were so ridiculously spicy that we had no choice but to throw the food away. On top of that, the rice was undercooked and clearly not fit to be served. This is basic food quality, and the restaurant failed badly.

When we complained to the waiter who took our order, instead of accepting the issue or resolving it properly, he started justifying it by saying the preparation was “Malvani,” so it is supposed to be spicy. We clearly told him that we are from Malvan and we know very well what authentic Malvani food tastes like. This was not authentic Malvani food at all — this was badly prepared, excessively spicy food with no balance and no proper understanding of the cuisine.

What made it even more insulting was that we were told the chef is Bengali, and yet the staff felt entitled to lecture us on Malvani food. That attitude was absolutely ridiculous.

The payment issue was equally shocking. We had booked through Zomato and had paid through Zomato, yet at the hotel they were forcing us to pay by cash or card again. If there was any such rule that thali orders had to be paid separately and not through Zomato, that should have been clearly communicated before placing the order. You cannot mislead customers first and then put them under pressure at the restaurant.

This is not even the first bad experience with this place. Earlier too, when I had ordered food from here, the spice level was so extreme that my parents actually had to take medical help. Because of that, I do not order from here for my parents anymore. Yes, a few dishes like Ghee Roast and Prawns Khichadi may be good, but that does not excuse the terrible quality and carelessness in several other dishes. Even the Seafood Hara Rassa soup appears to be deliberately made excessively spicy by adding too much black pepper.

I am sharing photos of the food we had to throw away because it was simply inedible — undercooked rice and gravies so spicy that they could not be consumed.

This kind of food quality, arrogant response, and misleading payment handling is completely unacceptable. A restaurant cannot hide behind the name of “Malvani food” to justify badly cooked and unbalanced food. Very disappointing experience.

Last weekend, I had the pleasure of dining at a delightful local restaurant that truly exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm smiles and genuine hospitality. The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive without being overbearing, which immediately set a welcoming tone for the evening.

The restaurant itself was neat, well-organized, and spotless—a rare and refreshing sight these days. Tables were clean, the atmosphere was cozy, and even the washrooms were well-maintained.

I ordered the mutton biryani and a lime soda, and both were absolutely spot-on. The biryani was aromatic and flavorful, with tender chunks of mutton that fell apart effortlessly. The spices were perfectly balanced—not too overpowering, but enough to leave a lasting impression. The lime soda was refreshing, tangy, and the perfect companion to the rich biryani.

What really stood out, aside from the great food, was how reasonably priced everything was. It's hard to find such quality and cleanliness at such affordable rates these days. Overall, this place is a gem for anyone looking for tasty food, a clean setting, and top-notch service without breaking the bank. I’ll definitely be coming back—and bringing friends along next time.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Subodh, 
Experiencing the flavors of the Konkan coast is truly what dining is all about, and it’s wonderful to hear that our seafood dishes resonated with you. The Bombil Fry and Butter Garlic Pepper Crab are favorites for a reason, and it’s delightful to know they stood out during your visit. Your pro tip about the "Catch of the Day" is sure to help other guests maximize their experience!
Regards, 
Mahesh Lunch Home

Oh! Calcutta, Andheri – A True Bengali Feast in Mumbai

I dropped by Oh! Calcutta in Andheri for a late lunch, and honestly, it was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in a while.

The restaurant is easy to find—right on the highway—and the vibe hits you as soon as you walk in. It’s warm, inviting, and has that polished-but-comfortable feel. When I was seated, I noticed these gorgeous white plates with vintage Bengali prints—they looked stunning and added a nice touch to the setting. Sadly, they’re just for show; you can’t actually eat off them. Still, great visual detail that sets the mood.

I was attended to immediately, seated without any delay, and the service from there on was top-notch. The waiter was not only attentive but genuinely helpful—he patiently answered all my questions and even walked me through their specials.

I started with the Calcutta Bhetki Fish Fry—boneless, buttery soft, and packed with flavor. It came with a mustard sauce and a curd-onion mix that completely stole the show. I even asked for a second helping of that mix—it was that good.

Next came the Gondhoraj Shorbot, made with a special lemon sourced from Bengal. The waiter recommended it, and I’m glad I listened. Refreshing, light, and a total palate cleanser. A hidden gem.

Then came the heavy hitters: Calcutta Mutton Biryani and Mutton Kosha. I’d always wanted to try their Kosha, but usually with luchi. This time, I asked if it would pair well with biryani, and the waiter said, “That’s the best combo.” He wasn’t wrong. The mutton kosha was incredible—thick, rich gravy with melt-in-the-mouth mutton. Easily the best I’ve ever had. And the biryani? Subtle, fragrant, and uniquely Bengali, with tender mutton, a boiled egg, and that signature baked potato. It’s not your typical masala-heavy biryani—it’s an acquired taste, but one I’ve come to love thanks to my Bengali friends over the years.

For dessert, I went with the Baked Rosogolla—another hit. The portion was smaller than expected, but it packed a punch. Baked with rabdi, it was warm, comforting, and a perfect end to the meal. Oh, and they even offered a complimentary paan on the way out. Nice touch.

Final verdict? Easily one of the best Bengali restaurants in Mumbai. Everything—from service to flavor—was on point. I’m already looking forward to my next visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Oh Calcutta..!
It's one of the most amazing place that I have been to for some authentic Bengali food 🐟.
There are many outlets in Mumbai of the restaurant like one in Tardeo, Andheri, Malad. I visited the outlet situated in Andheri West. The place is located just opposite to the Infiniti mall on the ground floor itself next to Mainland China and are interconnected from inside. So, the washroom 🚽 is only available in Mainland China so you have to enter Mainland China in order to go to the washroom . The ambience of restaurant was very soothing, you will find various painting 🖌️ hanging on the wall and the restraunt colour and furniture is white 🤍 and brown 🤎 in colour. Good old aesthetic effect to the restaurant.

It's a proper dining place, you will hear a soothing background music 🎶 going on, just a tuning. The staff 🤵 here are really helpful and well aware of the menu and the dishes. I really like that thing. So as I was trying Bengali menu for the first time I needed some help for which the staff recommended and guided me properly.  All the dishes which we tried most of it are recommended by the staff and I regretted ordering none of it. All the dishes were really good.

So we visited around 8-8:30PM at that time ⌚ it was empty which made me doubt the place but as the time goes by people 👪 started coming and it was the wonderful experience. On the table they will keep the plates 🍽️ already which has a design of Calcutta Howrah Bridge 🌉 further to serve the food they change the plate as it does not get damage and mix with your 🔥 hot food 🥣.

As soon as we ordered food, side dishes were brought to our table which included cucumber raita, Alu kabuli (kind of like potato and chickpea salad with some Indian masalas) and mustard kasundi (thick yellowish brown sauce with sharp taste made up of ground seeds of mustard plant). Side dishes were accompanying well with the starter and the main course that we ordered.

The following are dishes which we experienced here :

STARTERS
1. Murshidabadi murgi 🍗 : This is basically grilled chicken in Murshidabadi style. They are basically boneless chicken covered in Indian green paste and  spices. Was basically served as skewers. Overall it was tasting good but I would give a brownie point if some sort of chutney would have been served with it.  They will serve you onion 🧅 and lemon 🍋 if you ask them for it.

2. Bhetki Maccher Paturi 🐠: So bhetki is basically a river water which is sweet in taste 🐟. So basically they are steamed mustard fish parcels. The fish is covered with mustard and green chilli pasted and packed on banana leaf 🍃 and cooked by way of steam. They are boneless Bhetki fillets which makes it very easy to enjoy. The best dish that I had here. Must try.

REFRESHMENTS
3. Gondhoraj Shorbot: it’s a refreshing fragrant beverage made with ‘King of Lime’ 👑I.e Gondhoraj (big lemon grown in Kolkata which is popular for its frangrance and taste). Shorbot is basically like a sweet lime soda but you can definitely smell the different aroma from the drink. 🍋🥤

4. Watermelon and Basil crush: it’s fresh basil 🌿 burst with juicy watermelon chunks 🍉infused with aerated drink 🍹 . It was very refreshing. ☺️Amongst both the mocktails, I loved watermelon mocktail. It’s worth trying.

MAIN COURSE
4.  Kancha lonka murgi 🍗 : So it's a Bengali style chicken with a dry green gravy made up of fresh coriander and chillies. If you have never tried green 💚 chicken then this is worth trying. I'll not recommend having rice with this gravy. Even the staff suggested not to order rice with it as the gravy is thick but still I wanted to try it with rice (so the staff offered us half portion of rice without charge, it was such a good gesture we loved it 🥰)

5. Luchi : So luchi is basically a puffed up puri made of maida (refined wheat flour). Very thin and soft in texture. It is similar to bhature but made without using dahi. You can try it with any gravy.

DESERT

featured_reviews.name: Abhi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Foo, Andheri for a Pan-Asian meal at lunch time . The ambience is definitely one of the highlights — stylish interiors, good lighting, and a lively vibe that works well but still did not find it something out of the box or extraordinary.

The menu has a wide variety of Asian dishes, which is impressive, and the presentation of the food is However okayish for me. At best the food was 6/10 for me.

However, the overall experience was a bit inconsistent. Some dishes tasted good while others felt average for the price point. Portion sizes also felt very small considering the cost.i mean 4 pcs for an 800₹ sushi is too much.
Service was polite but slow at times, and we had to wait longer than expected for a few items.

Overall, it’s a decent place for ambience and variety, but the food has to be more consistent to fully justify the pricing. An okay experience, but there’s room for improvement.

For me , personally this is not a must visit place.

featured_reviews.name: Kiran Bovane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing experience at Sorozai on Versova Beach Road! If you’re looking for authentic Goan food, this place absolutely delivers. Every dish tasted like it came straight from Goa.

The Mutton Cutlet was easily one of the best I’ve ever had perfectly cooked, flavorful, and packed with authentic taste. The Calamari Golden Fry was crispy, fresh, and incredibly addictive.

The real star of the meal, though, was the Prawns Roshel. Honestly, they were some of the tastiest prawns I’ve ever eaten—perfectly seasoned and bursting with flavor.

The drinks are a little on the pricey side, but still affordable and worth it considering the quality of the food and overall experience.

To make the evening even better, the staff surprised us with a complimentary Caramel Custard for dessert. It was a thoughtful gesture and a perfect sweet ending to an already fantastic meal.

Highly recommended for anyone craving genuine Goan cuisine in Mumbai. Will definitely be coming back!

featured_reviews.name: Debashis Dey
featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to Sorozai felt like a quiet escape into the flavours and soul of Goa. The cuisine is deeply rooted in tradition, yet presented with a certain understated finesse.
The prawns in richado sauce were a highlight... bold, tangy, and beautifully spiced, perfectly paired with soft, fresh poee, the classic Goan bread. The chilli pork carried just the right balance of heat and depth, making it both comforting and indulgent. Complemented by well-crafted cocktails, the meal felt complete and thoughtfully curated.
What truly elevates the experience is the candle-lit ambience... intimate, warm, and inviting.. paired with excellent service and genuinely smiling staff who make you feel at ease from the moment you walk in.
A place that doesn’t just serve food, but quietly recreates a mood... Sorozai is a must-visit for anyone seeking authentic Goan flavours with a touch of charm.

featured_reviews.name: Shruti Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving the charm of a laid-back Goan shack without leaving Mumbai, this place absolutely nails the vibe. From the atmosphere to the food, it feels like a little Goa escape in the middle of the city.

Here’s what we tried:
Prawn Risois – 3/5
Calamari Rings – 2/5
Goan Prawn Curry – 5/5
Amboli – 1/5 (honestly felt more like a dosa)
Poie – 2/5 (a little too dense for my liking)

But the absolute star of the meal was the Goan Prawn Curry. Comforting, flavourful, and exactly what you’d expect from a good Goan meal. YOU HAVE TO TRY IT.

Ended the meal with their brownie ice cream dessert, which was a total banger finisher after the hearty curry experience.

featured_reviews.name: Uneza Kohli
featured_reviews.review_text: Soroziae at Seven Bungalows in Andheri West is such a vibe, especially in the evening when the whole place gives you proper Goa feels with warm lighting, great music and a relaxed coastal energy. Being a Goan bar and restaurant, the menu really reflects that authenticity and what I loved most is that they have something special happening every single day, which keeps it exciting if you like trying new experiences. It’s one of those places where you can just unwind, enjoy good food and drinks, and soak in the atmosphere without it feeling overdone.

featured_reviews.name: Mishti Khadye
featured_reviews.review_text:
Walking into Sorosai feels like stepping into a Goa time capsule — and the best part? It’s smacked right opposite Versova beach! 🌊

Getting there
Pro tip: Grab a sharing auto outside Versova metro, solo rides can take time.

Ambiance
Best time? Sunset. Staff told me the sea view’s the real star. The entrance is a riot of colour, but step inside and it’s vintage Goa chic: dim lights, old-school feels, and nostalgia on tap. My mom (Goa born-and-raised) was practically reliving her childhood 😭. Spot on vibe.

Hospitality
HUGE shoutout to the waiters and managers — attentive, considerate, and if you speak Konkani, they’ll geek out with you. Feels like you’re in Goa, not Andheri.

Food & Drinks
Everything we tried = chef’s kiss 💯
Drinks: Susegad Punch was subtle yet super flavourful. Kokum Soda? Crazy refreshing.

Mains: Prawn Balchao with poi had a burst of flavours — perfectly spicy, flavourful with that right sour kick. Hirva Fry Skillet Pomfret was unreal — fish was fresh and the green stuffing was exactly how I imagined it.

Desserts: Tender Coconut Panna Cotta & Caramel Custard just hit the right spot. Made fresh by them and something you definitely have to try!

Photography
I loved the vibe & the pictures/videos came out great even with dim lights✨

Overall: If you’re craving a Goa escape , Soro zai’s your spot.

featured_reviews.name: Kaushik Kolhapure
featured_reviews.review_text:
Soro Zai, Versova (Aaram Nagar) is a hidden gem if you’re craving authentic Goan flavours in the city. The place has a relaxed, artsy vibe that instantly makes you feel at ease.

Their Goan delicacies are the highlight rich, comforting, and full of coastal flavour. The fresh seafood really stands out, perfectly cooked and super fresh, just the way it should be. Pair it with their well crafted cocktails, and it just elevates the whole experience.

Service is warm and easygoing, adding to the overall chill vibe of the place. It’s perfect for a laid back evening with good food, great drinks, and even better company.

If you’re around Versova and love seafood + Goan cuisine, Soro Zai is definitely worth a visit. 🐟🍹

featured_reviews.name: San Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
When a place keeps the menu limited, it’s either risky… or legendary. And this one? Legendary when it comes to food.

Every single dish served was crafted to perfection — bold flavors, perfect seasoning, and beautifully presented. It’s rare to order multiple items and have everything taste exceptional. The flavor? A solid 10/10. Absolutely unforgettable.

That said, the portions are on the smaller side and the prices are definitely on the higher end. The beverages are also quite pricey.

They do add a 10% service charge (which they will remove if requested). The service was okay — nothing major to complain about — but it didn’t justify a fixed 10% charge, so we chose to have it removed and instead paid a tip that matched the level of service provided.

Overall: limited menu, smaller portions, expensive drinks — but outstanding taste.  🍽️🔥

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has become a personal favorite when it comes to seafood—I've been a regular here, and it never disappoints!

The variety they offer is fantastic, and the quality is consistently top-notch. Despite the 1+1 seating setup, the place is always crowded, which speaks volumes about how popular it is. If you're a fan of South Indian-style seafood, you're in for a treat—their preparations really stand out.

Some dishes you must try include the Seafood Soup, the rich and flavorful Seafood Gassi, and the tangy Pulli Munchi. We were also recommended the Prawns Kadipatta—it was absolutely delicious. If you’re into crab, they’ve got some great options there too!

What I love most is that it's not just tasty, but also easy on the wallet. Great seafood, great flavors, and great value—what more can you ask for?

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options.

I recently visited Global Fusion Versova, and it was a delightful experience! They had an impressive variety of starters — around 15 options each for both veg and non-veg lovers, with unique and flavorful selections that really stood out. Perfect for anyone who enjoys exploring new tastes!

The main course was equally satisfying, and the desserts added a sweet finishing touch to the meal. The ambience was pleasant and welcoming, making the overall experience even better.

If you're someone who loves to try different starters and enjoy a good meal in a nice environment, I would definitely recommend visiting this place!

featured_reviews.name: Mehndi Baig
featured_reviews.review_text: I went to Global Fusion Restaurant for dinner yesterday and absolutely loved the experience! The food was amazing – each and every dish I tried was top-class and full of flavor. The ambience was really nice, and it added to the overall dining experience. The staff was very kind and helpful, which made me feel really comfortable. I personally don’t like sushi, so I skipped that, but everything else was outstanding. Truly enjoyed my time here and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a great buffet experience!

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Global Fusion at Versova for lunch and had a delightful experience. This place is a paradise for foodies—especially if you’re someone with a big appetite or a love for non-vegetarian dishes. The spread is massive, offering more than 20 starters served right to your table, a wide-ranging buffet, a tempting dessert counter, and complimentary beverages, which add great value to the overall experience.

If you love sushi, this is definitely the place for you. They offer unlimited sushi with various options, and everything is freshly prepared and well-presented. The seafood selection is also impressive—with dishes featuring prawns, bhetki, and crab that are cooked to perfection. The prawn tempura and dumplings were personal favorites.

The ambiance is warm and spacious, ideal for group lunches, celebrations, or casual family meals. The staff was polite and attentive, ensuring a smooth dining experience.

Having dined earlier at the Worli branch, I personally felt the food quality and taste there were slightly better compared to the Versova outlet, especially in terms of seasoning and presentation. However, that doesn’t take away from the fact that Versova still offers great value and variety.

Overall, if you’re a non veg lover or someone who enjoys variety in a buffet, Global Fusion Versova is worth a visit. Great food, vibrant vibe, and plenty to indulge in!

I came from Germany to visit this place and after I had already a mediocre experience in another restaurant the other day, I wanted to opt for an all you can eat buffet. As an athlete that generally just eats one big meal a day, this is crucial for my performance and the quality of food isn't lacking any deficits here.

The sushi was well prepared and the different kinds of flavors one can experience here is above average.

As you can see, there's a wide variety of options for non veg to veg to vegan. The service was optimal and I was treated really kindly, especially by the restaurant manager Shetty and Mister Raj. I was even given an iced tea, on the house. I generally don't consume sugary drinks but it was very good and highly appreciated as an act of kindness!

It's definitely worth the price if you feel like having a buffet in a good and calm area in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Something’s Fishy last week to celebrate a family friend’s birthday.

If you’re a seafood lover, Something’s Fishy is the kind of place that instantly feels right. From the moment you step in, the ambience sets the mood. The interiors have a beautiful seafood-inspired theme, artistically done without being over the top. Subtle marine elements, thoughtful décor, and warm lighting make the space feel relaxed and inviting. It’s comfortable enough for a family dinner yet stylish enough for a special outing.

We tried quite a variety of dishes, and honestly, the experience from start to finish was satisfying.

Harra Channa ka Shorba (Chicken Soup): A comforting, mildly spiced chicken soup with fresh herb flavours. Light yet flavourful, it had a soothing warmth and well-balanced seasoning, perfect to begin the meal.

Chicken Gassi: Rich, coastal-style chicken curry with aromatic spices and creamy coconut base. The gravy was flavourful without being overpowering, and the chicken pieces were tender and well-cooked.

Appams: Soft, fluffy appams with delicate crisp edges. Light texture and subtle sweetness paired beautifully with the gassi gravies, soaking up flavours perfectly without becoming soggy.

Prawn Gassi: Fresh prawns cooked in traditional coastal gravy with coconut and spices. The prawns were juicy and tender, absorbing the rich masala while retaining their natural sweetness.

Butter Garlic Prawn: Perfectly sautéed prawns tossed in butter and garlic. Simple yet delicious, with a lovely aroma and balanced seasoning that allowed the freshness of the seafood to shine.

Surmai Fry: Crispy on the outside, moist and flaky inside. The fish was fresh, well-marinated, and fried just right, delivering bold coastal flavours without excessive oiliness.

Rawas Tandoori: Well-marinated rawas grilled to perfection in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, and packed with spices, yet the fish remained soft and flavourful inside.

Squid Crispy Fried Rings: Lightly battered squid rings fried till crisp. Crunchy outside, tender inside, with balanced seasoning that made them addictive without feeling too heavy.

What stood out throughout the meal was the freshness of the seafood. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, not rushed. Portions were generous, and the flavours felt authentic rather than overly commercialised.

Service was smooth and friendly. The staff were attentive, happy to recommend dishes, and ensured everything was served at the right pace. They didn’t hover unnecessarily, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, Something’s Fishy delivers exactly what you expect from a seafood speciality restaurant — fresh ingredients, authentic coastal flavours, and a warm, pleasant ambience. It’s definitely a place I’d revisit whenever seafood cravings strike. Highly recommended for anyone who truly enjoys well-prepared seafood.

Our team is committed to providing authentic seafood in Mumbai, and your feedback encourages us to continue delivering the best quality seafood every day.

For appetisers, the highlight was definitely the Butter Garlic Crab—easily my favourite of the night, fresh, flavourful, and cooked to perfection. We also tried the Chicken Peri Peri Tikka, which came sizzling on a live grill—juicy, spicy, and packed with flavour.

Moving on to mains, the Prawns Tawa Masala was a total Mumbaiya flavour bomb—rich, spicy, and incredibly satisfying. The Chicken Makhanwala paired beautifully with soft Garlic Naan, making for a comforting and indulgent combo.

And don’t even think of leaving without dessert—the Pull Me Up Lotus Biscoff Cheesecake is heavenly and the perfect sweet ending to the meal.
Highly recommend this place for anyone craving fresh, delicious seafood with a fine-dining experience! 🍤✨

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place has a G+2 seating arrangement—non-AC on the ground floor and AC seating on the first and second floors. Seating is decent.

Unlike many traditional bars, no complimentary chakna is served here. Alcohol prices felt on the higher side, and the 180 ml vodka was served from a larger container instead of a sealed bottle, which was a bit disappointing. Mixers were limited to Coke and Sprite only. Initially, staff said outside mixers would be charged extra, but after speaking to the manager, they allowed to buy it from outside without any charge.

Service was decent but not very attentive, especially towards regular or light drinkers—attention seemed more focused on heavy customers.

Coming to food: Apple Chicken was good, and the green kokani/malvani-style kairi chutney served with it was unique and delicious. We ordered Chicken Thali (₹300) and Mutton Thali (₹430). Quantity felt slightly less for the price—total four pieces (two gravy, two fry). Taste-wise, chicken and mutton gravies and fries had almost the same masala, which reduced variety.

Ambience is decent overall, but the washroom ceiling is quite low, which can be uncomfortable for tall people.

Overall, a decent experience—good chutney and some dishes stand out, but quantity, attention to service, and a few basic facilities can definitely improve.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this restaurant mainly because the name included “Gomantak”, expecting decent seafood. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a huge disappointment.
We ordered pomfret fry, prawns masala, mushroom chilli, and roti. The waiting time was almost one hour, which was already frustrating. When the food finally arrived, the experience only got worse.
The pomfret fry was absolutely bland, with no salt or spices—completely tasteless and frankly pathetic. The prawns masala was just okay, nothing special and far from what you’d expect from a place claiming coastal flavors. Mushroom chilli and rotis were average at best.
Overall, a regretful visit. The food quality and taste did not justify the long wait or the expectations set by the restaurant’s name. Definitely not worth it and would not recommend.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

Overall, the ambience and company made the experience enjoyable, but food-wise, only a few dishes really stood out for us.

featured_reviews.name: hemali kantharia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our go-to family dinner spot for any and every occasion. From small celebrations to casual dinners, this place has always been our first choice. Over time we’ve tried almost everything on the menu, and every visit somehow turns into another food memory with family.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Mitesh Parmar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was the final restaurant I attended on my trip and a great place to end on.

Unfortunately at the time of our attendance the A/C was not in working order which the manager/owner advised on prior to entering, however we still went in as they had fans going on.

Didn't plan to eat a lot but to take in the delights on offer as again this was a place recommended.

We were given good information by the manager on some of the dishes and on ordering the food arrived after a short time. temperatures were on point and flavours were amazing. The prawn starters were so good, especially the Prawns Garlic Butter, so much so we ordered another tray. I also order the Mutton Chops Ghee Roast and as it sat in front of me my mouth was watering. Spice level on this was perfect, had a nice little kick but was really enjoyable and not in a overpowering way. featured_reviews.name: Nisikant Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Gajalee recently for seafood, and the experience was mixed. While the restaurant has a strong reputation and offers a wide variety of seafood (including crab, pomfret, oysters, and even snails), the pricing feels significantly inflated for what is essentially a standard dining setup.

For instance, crab was quoted at around ₹5000 per kg (pre-processing), and a medium-sized pomfret fry, recommended by the staff—cost about ₹2000. The taste was decent, but not proportionate to the premium pricing.

The restaurant tends to be overcrowded in the evenings, likely due to limited seafood options in the surrounding area, drawing local seafood enthusiasts. However, compared to coastal cities like Visakhapatnam, Chennai, Bhubaneswar, Kolkata, or Kochi, the prices here are almost double without a corresponding difference in quality or experience.

Overall, it may appeal to those specifically seeking seafood in this locality, but in terms of value for money, it falls short.
N.B: After having Pomfret, I have been suffering from stomach upset (Food poisoning) and currently recovering.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an absolutely fantastic Malvani seafood lunch at Malwani Aswad in Vile Parle East. The best part about this place is how close the flavours are to authentic homemade Malvani/Konkani food, rich, fresh, and 100% true to the cuisine. The menu has a huge variety, and it’s rare to find places serving premium fish like Chonak, depending on availability of course.
We started with Tisrya Sukha, and it was bursting with flavour — fleshy clams and a sukha masala that was an absolute banger. The Bombil Fry, Chonak Fry, and Prawns Fry were all incredibly fresh and perfectly fried. The Surmai curry was beautifully balanced, and the Solkadhi paired wonderfully with the meal. Had it all with bhakri and a little rice, and the portions were very generous.
The restaurant is small, but spotlessly clean, very well maintained, and clearly run with a lot of passion. You may have to wait during peak hours, but it is 100% worth the wait. Special shoutout to the owners for serving such authentic flavours with consistency and care. Wishing you bigger success ahead  truly one of the best Malvani food experiences in Mumbai. 🌊🐟🔥

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Revisited this little seafood spot after 6–7 years and it felt like meeting an old friend who hasn’t changed one bit, in the best way possible.
The space is still compact (barely 4-5 tables, seating around 18–20 people), but the addition of A/C is a welcome upgrade.

The menu is limited, but honestly, you’re here for the thalis—and they absolutely deliver. The prawns thali was the highlight: 2 chapatis, rice, a soulful fish curry, 7–8 small fried prawns, jawla, salad, cabbage, and sol kadi. Everything was simple, balanced, and deeply satisfying. The curry stood out—rich, comforting, and packed with flavour—while the sol kadi was fresh and refreshingly light.

The chicken thali didn’t lag behind either. The curry was delicious, paired perfectly with the usual sides—rice, chapati, salad, and sol kadi—making it a wholesome, no-fuss meal.

We also tried the bombil fry, which came perfectly crispy and fresh—exactly how it should be.

At just ₹760 for two, this place is unbelievably economical. Add to that the warm, friendly staff, and you’ve got yourself a true hidden gem in Juhu.

The staff serve with genuine smiles and even check if you’d like a little top-up of food — a lovely touch that makes you feel cared for. The food is simple, fresh, tasty, and unbelievably value for money. Far from fancy, but full of heart. Perfect spot for a quiet, homely seafood meal served with warmth and authenticity.

featured_reviews.name: chaturved falari
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic Goan seafood that takes you straight to the beaches of Goa, Goa Bhavan in Juhu is a hidden gem you cannot miss! From the moment I walked in, the homely vibe and subtle aroma of freshly prepared seafood set the tone for an amazing experience.

The Prawns chilly was a delightful explosion of flavors—perfectly marinated with tangy masala that hit all the right notes. The Pomfret Thali was the star of the show—succulent fish fried to perfection, accompanied by a medley of traditional Goan sides that balanced the spices and textures beautifully.

I also tried the Bombil Fry and Surmay Fry, both incredibly crispy and seasoned just right, preserving the natural taste of the seafood without overpowering it. Every bite transported me back to a Goan kitchen where food is cooked with love and authenticity.

What sets Goa Bhavan apart is the attention to detail and consistency in taste—just like homemade Goan food, but served with finesse. The service was prompt and courteous, and the ambiance added to the overall warmth.

Whether you’re a seafood enthusiast or simply love trying traditional regional cuisine, Goa Bhavan promises a meal that’s rich, satisfying, and truly memorable. Highly recommended!❤️✨

Ordered one prrawn thali, a Surmai thali and bombil tawa fry.We were utterly disappointed with the portion, size of the bombil fish and also the overall masala taste of the dish.Coming to the thalis initially 4 small Surmai pieces were served which we asked them to replace and to which they immediately obliged with a proper large Surmai piece (which was promised by the attendant while placing the order) but again we were served the thinnest possible Surmai piece an absolute shame for the price.A big turnoff  again!!
As the charges for thali was 775/- for both Surmai and Prawn thali.Atleast they could have served a decent size of the fish.Also to make it worse the rassa(fish curry )is not a exclusive or of a  particular fish,they serve a common fish curry in all fish thalis which again was a bit bitter totally lacking aroma and taste.Also their are times when you want to have a good time and experience visiting such places and are in no mood to indulge in any altercation spoiling the mood.
However the only food we enjoyed, were the appetizers cum accompaniments provided on arrival - papads, mango chutney was excellent.WE thoroughly enjoyed only that!!Never coming back nor recommending anyone.
TEMPTATIONS THOROUGHLY DESTROYED!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience was top class, and the seating was extremely comfortable. Since the restaurant is not located in a crowded area, the overall atmosphere was calm and peaceful. Even during peak lunch hours, there was no waiting time or rush inside, which made the dining experience very relaxing.
The staff were exceptional and truly made us feel pampered. They paid attention to every small detail, especially when we mentioned our prawn allergy. Extra care was taken to ensure our dishes were prepared and served safely, which we really appreciated.
Unfortunately, crab was not available that day, apparently, it’s one of their best dishes. However, our main intention was to try Bombil, and we were not disappointed. We ordered Bombil fry and Bombil masala. More than just the taste, it was the overall experience that made the meal so memorable. The masala was flavourful and delicious, and I absolutely loved it. The Bombil fry was just okay for me, as it felt a bit bland especially to a Malayali palate that’s used to richer, more robust masalas. However, I did want to experience this style of preparation, and in that sense, it was still a good and interesting experience. Overall, a wonderful dining experience and definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Dabholkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is very nice, clean, and well-maintained. The staff was courteous, attentive, and provided excellent service throughout our visit.

We initially wanted to order Bombil Fry but were unsure about their preparation style, so we hesitated. Based on the staff's recommendation, we ordered the Prawns Green Chilly Masala, Tisrya Masala, and Tandoori Pomfret. The food was served quickly, and to our surprise, the staff thoughtfully brought us two complimentary pieces of Bombil Fry as a tasting sample.

The Bombil Fry was exactly the way we like it—crispy, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. We immediately ordered a full portion, and the green chutney served with it was outstanding and complemented the fish perfectly.

Every dish we ordered was delicious, but the Tandoori Pomfret was the clear winner—perfectly cooked, juicy, and packed with flavor. We ended our meal with Solkadhi, which was decent but average in taste compared to the excellent food.

Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience with great food, warm hospitality, and thoughtful customer service. I would definitely recommend this place, especially for seafood lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Pradnya Pawaskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
One star only because Google won’t let me post without giving one. Gajalee, Marol is easily one of the most overrated and disappointing restaurants I’ve ever visited. Honestly, even a roadside stall serves food with more taste, quantity, and value than this place. GAJALEE, please consider shutting down and stop scaming people in name of Malvani food, its a sheer insult to the cuisine.
We visited for lunch today and ordered the basics — Bombil Fry (₹525) and a Surmai Thali. The Bombil Fry arrived as two tiny, overstuffed pieces drowned in oil. Absolutely ridiculous for the price. The actual food on that plate probably wasn’t even worth ₹50. Zero taste, zero quality, and absolutely zero value for money.
Then came the so-called Surmai Thali — shockingly, it didn’t even include fried surmai. Instead, it had fish curry with one tiny boiled piece of surmai, the curry tasted no where even close to Maharashtrian style, some bean sabzi, two random pieces of bombil fry (seriously, who puts bombil in a Surmai Thali?), and solkadhi. Completely pathetic and a total waste of money.
The experience was so bad that we lost all interest in eating there and ended up going to another restaurant nearby to have lunch again.
The staff couldn’t care less. For almost 20 minutes, nobody even bothered coming to our table to take an order or check on us. The entire place runs on hype and fake reviews. We regret spending 1500 for something that was not worth for a value.
Please do not fall for the ratings or reviews online. This place is an absolute scam in the name of seafood dining.
